title: ZPA Terraform resources: fields not sent, not read back, or written in several non-atomic steps
aliases: terraform zpa state does not match api
service edge assistant schedule destroy does nothing
user code verification failed after create
server group name blank on update
zia cloud config read error ignored

prose.text: Several ZPA resources do not do what their schema promises: an argument is dropped on the way out, a response field is dropped on the way back, or one logical write is split into several requests with no way back. Application segment resources have their own version of this problem in [[zpa.terraform.app-segment-lifecycle]].

checks.do: Whether the remote object matches the configuration after an apply on these resources, by reading it from the API rather than trusting state.
Whether the remote schedule setting is read directly after create, import or destroy, since an empty resource ID is the first symptom of the create path.
Whether the object exists and holds the first request's changes before a failed multi-request write is retried.
Whether an imported provisioning key of an association type the import does not probe was actually found, rather than assuming its type was read.

The request ID is read from the resource's own computed `id`. Only the already-exists branch sets an ID taken from the server, by reading the singleton schedule.

private-cloud-create-then-fire-drill-put.statement: Creating a private cloud with fire drill enabled is two writes. The provider clears `FireDrillEnabled` and the fire drill site from the POST, then sends them in a separate PUT after storing the new ID. If that PUT fails, the provider returns an error that says the cloud was created and to run apply again; it does not delete the cloud. The provider's comments say the API rejects fire drill on create; that is the provider's statement, not shown here.

stale-state-hides-out-of-band-removal.statement: Where a Read sets a block only inside a condition on the response, a block or capability removed out of band leaves the previous value in state, so a plan can show no difference from a configuration that still holds it.
stale-state-hides-out-of-band-removal.conditions: Assumes the plan compares the configuration with the refreshed state and that the configuration still holds the removed value; that plan behavior is Terraform core, not shown by these sources.

refresh-from-list-index.statement: From v4.4.13 (#694), refresh of application segments, application servers, segment groups, server groups, App Connector groups and the v1/v2 access, timeout and forwarding policy rules reads each object from one paginated list fetched per run and per microtenant, instead of one GET per object. App Connector groups read only from the list, also after create and update. For the other types the provider reads an object by ID when the list call fails or the object is not in the list, and create and update read the object back individually.

quotes: now refresh from their paginated list endpoint (500 objects per page), fetched once per run and per microtenant, instead of making one API request per resource
[PR #694](https://github.com/zscaler/terraform-provider-zpa/pull/694) - Improved `terraform plan` and refresh performance for large configurations.
A resource that is not in the list is read individually before it is removed from state, except `zpa_app_connector_group`, which reads only from the list as before.
Create and update still read the resource back individually.

api-server-group-put-name.title: How ZPA treats a server group PUT that has no name
api-server-group-put-name.blocks: saying whether an ordinary server group update blanks, keeps or rejects the name
api-server-group-put-name.detail: The client sends no name member when only other attributes changed. Whether ZPA keeps the stored name, clears it or returns an error is not shown by any captured source. Test in a scratch tenant: change only the description of a server group through Terraform and re-read the name.

api-approval-window-validation.title: Whether the ZPA API rejects a privileged approval whose end is before its start
api-approval-window-validation.blocks: saying whether a backwards approval window is caught at all
api-approval-window-validation.detail: Unverified statement: The approval validator runs at apply, so a backwards window is reported by the API, if at all, not by the provider. The provider validator is read in pra-approval-end-not-checked-against-start; the OpenAPI approval operations give startTime and endTime as plain integers with no stated ordering rule. What would resolve it: create an approval with an end before its start in a scratch tenant and record the response.

list-vs-get-field-parity.title: Whether list responses carry every field the by-ID GET returns for the nine list-refreshed resource types
list-vs-get-field-parity.detail: From v4.4.13 refresh state for these types comes from the list endpoint (refresh-from-list-index). If a list response omits or summarizes a field the by-ID response carries, refreshed state can differ from what a by-ID read would have written, which would show as a plan difference after upgrading. No source here compares the two response shapes per type.
list-vs-get-field-parity.blocks: saying that refresh fidelity is unchanged by the v4.4.13 upgrade
